tasks.short: Read the prescription, ask about work, hobbies and screen use, evaluate the prescription against those needs, and note them on the client card.

steps.what: Optician asks the client about vocational and avocational visual requirements
Optician evaluates prescriptions in conjunction with the client's needs
Optician notes the needs on the client card

tasks.design: Prescriptions from optometrists and eye doctors arrive in the shop system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) through secure messaging instead of on paper, so they are not read and retyped. Visual needs (screen distance, driving, sports) go into structured fields on the client card. Asking about needs and evaluating the prescription stay with the optician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prescriptions came on paper and needs were noted in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Shop systems take electronic prescriptions and hold structured client cards.
tasks.still_hard: Prescriptions from abroad still come on paper.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing that a client's hobby needs a different reading distance.

evidence.claim: Shop systems can take electronic prescriptions and hold structured client cards.
Health data are special category data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from the prescription to needs noted; the lens choice is outside.
Input contract: prescribers send electronically; fallback is paper.

incremental.description: Optician enters paper prescriptions that still arrive.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many paper prescriptions; high: mostly electronic prescriptions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend lenses, coatings and frames, look up lens options and prices, and prepare the quote.

steps.what: Optician recommends specific lenses, lens coatings and frames to suit client needs
Optician looks up lens options and prices in supplier catalogues

tasks.design: A lens configurator in the shop system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) loads the suppliers' price files and shows only the lenses and coatings available for the client's prescription range, with prices, so the optician does not search catalogues. The quote is generated from the chosen options. Recommending what suits the client stays with the optician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lens options and prices were looked up in several catalogues and quotes written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Lens suppliers publish price files that configurators can load.
tasks.still_hard: Special lenses are outside standard price files.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining why a cheaper lens will do for a client's needs.
tasks.altitude: The optician advises instead of searching catalogues.

reach.learn: Whether quotes are clear and quick.

evidence.claim: Lens configurators can load supplier price files and filter by prescription range.

assumptions: Boundary: from needs noted to the quote made; the order is outside.
Input contract: supplier price files kept current; fallback is catalogues.

incremental.description: Optician loads new supplier price files.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many special lenses; high: mostly standard lenses.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Help the client choose frames by style and colour, take facial and eye measurements, and check the frame against the prescription.

steps.what: Optician assists clients in selecting frames according to style and color
Optician takes facial and eye measurements by hand
Optician checks that frames are coordinated with the optical prescription

tasks.design: A digital centration device takes pupil distance and fitting heights from a photo of the client wearing the frame and sends them to the work order, so they are not measured with a ruler and typed. The configurator shows the expected lens thickness for the chosen frame and prescription. Helping the client choose and judging the fit stay with the optician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measurements were taken with a ruler and lens thickness estimated from experience.
tasks.enabler_now: Centration devices measure from photos; configurators compute lens thickness.
tasks.still_hard: Children and some clients cannot hold still for the photo.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which frame makes a client feel good.

reach.learn: Whether remakes for wrong measurements fall.

evidence.claim: Digital centration devices measure pupil distance and fitting heights from photos.

assumptions: Boundary: from the quote to the frame checked; lens production is outside.
Input contract: centration device linked to the shop system; fallback is a ruler.
Choosing frames stays with the client and optician.

incremental.description: Optician measures by hand when the photo fails.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many children; high: mostly adults with standard frames.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enter prescriptions, write work orders for lenses, check the order, send it to the lens lab, record payments and insurer claims, and file records.

steps.what: Optician enters customer prescriptions into the shop system from paper
Optician writes work orders for lenses
Optician checks the final work order
Optician sends the lens order to the lab by phone or e-mail
Optician maintains records of payments and insurer claims

tasks.design: Electronic prescriptions land in the shop system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), and the work order fills from the prescription, measurements and chosen lens. Once the optician has checked the order, it goes to the lens lab's ordering system through the integration instead of by phone or e-mail. The payment terminal is linked to the sale, and insurer claims go as standard messages from the shop system. Records are kept digitally, so paper is not filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prescriptions were retyped, orders phoned or mailed and payments booked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Shop systems link prescriptions, lab ordering, payments and insurer claims.
tasks.still_hard: Small lens labs lack ordering links.
tasks.human_edge: Catching a prescription that does not match what the client said.
tasks.altitude: The optician checks orders instead of retyping them.

evidence.claim: Shop systems can link prescriptions, lab ordering, payment terminals and insurer claims.
Medical records are kept and shared only with consent; fax is not used for sharing.

assumptions: Boundary: from the prescription to records filed; lens production is outside.
Input contract: lab and insurer links available; fallback is phone, e-mail and paper.
The lab handles electronic orders as it did phoned ones.

incremental.description: Optician resolves orders the lab link rejects.

approvals.approved_version: The work order as checked by the optician in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many paper prescriptions and small labs; high: electronic prescriptions and linked labs.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The optician keeps evaluating needs, recommending lenses and helping clients choose frames; retyped prescriptions, catalogue searches, ruler measurements and paper records shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the lens configurator and centration device
role.ambitious_version: An optician with more time with clients.
